clue.text: Stimulate with hot film

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with
H for hot, as on a tap
E.T. is Spielberg's 1982 film

explanation.surface: Someone is aroused by a steamy movie.
explanation.definitionFit: To whet the appetite is to sharpen or arouse it, a close synonym of stimulate.

clue.text: Shade in haunted house where the symbols match

parts.note: the word to compare against: it shares an H, a U and an E with the next word and nothing else

indicators.note: the symbols are letters, so we keep only the characters the two words have in common

parts.note: the letters house has in common with haunted, which happen to be its 1st, 3rd and 5th

explanation.surface: A ghostly shadow falls inside a haunted house where everything is eerily paired.
explanation.walkthrough: Haunted and house both contain an H, a U and an E, and no other letter appears in both.
explanation.definitionFit: A hue is a tint or variety of colour, which is one sense of shade.

clue.text: Botching run, stay on like a despot

indicators.note: botching a job means making a mess of it, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bungled election campaign sees a leader cling on like a dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrannous means ruling cruelly and absolutely, which is how a despot behaves.

clue.text: Foolishly queries tip as fringe benefit

indicators.note: something done foolishly is done without order or sense, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone unwisely asks whether a gratuity counts as a workplace perk.
explanation.definitionFit: A perquisite, or perk, is an extra advantage given on top of salary.

clue.text: Portion at heart oddly peripheral

indicators.note: oddly tells us to keep the characters in the first, third, fifth and later odd positions

parts.note: the 1st, 3rd, 5th letters and so on across the three words

explanation.surface: Reads like a medical note about a slice of tissue at the edge of the heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peripheral' looks like an adjective, but here it is the computing noun: a device attached to a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A printer is a classic computer peripheral, an external device plugged into the machine.

clue.text: Assemble kit in a good mood

parts.note: a rig is a set of equipment
feeling up means cheerful

explanation.surface: Someone happily puts together a flat-pack kit.
explanation.definitionFit: To rig up something is to assemble or construct it, often in makeshift fashion.

clue.text: Cheerful small gestures from the conductor

parts.note: upbeat means optimistic
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: An orchestra leader makes happy little waves of the baton.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeats are the unaccented beats a conductor marks with an upward movement of the baton.

clue.text: Doctor loves what you do

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A physician adores their work.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition addresses you, the solver: what you do with this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Solving a clue is exactly the activity the person reading the crossword is engaged in.

clue.text: Old bag from Turkey available for purchase

parts.note: TR is the international code for Turkey
a new book that is out can be bought

explanation.surface: A vintage handbag from Istanbul is up for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old bag' looks like a handbag, but it is the insult for an unpleasant older woman, which in British slang is also an old trout.
explanation.definitionFit: Old trout is British slang for a bad-tempered elderly woman, the same insult as old bag.

clue.text: Craving the last bit of stretchy netting

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final character only

parts.note: the end of stretchy
to net money is to earn it

explanation.surface: Someone longs for the final scrap of elastic mesh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Netting' looks like mesh fabric but is the verb net, to take home as pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearning is a strong longing or desire, the same as a craving.

clue.text: Later on interrupted by large blast of hot air

indicators.note: something interrupted has another thing breaking into its middle

parts.note: in a document, below means further on
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A windbag's long speech is cut short by a big gust.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellow is a loud roar, a noisy outburst that could be called a blast of hot air.

clue.text: What attracts spy chief? Agent whose hidden opponents flip

indicators.note: the pair of bridge opponents sitting inside the word turn over, so that pair reads the other way

parts.note: M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories
taken as written; its inner E and N are East and North, opponents at bridge

explanation.surface: An espionage thriller: the spymaster suspects an agent of secretly switching sides.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North-South play against East-West, so the adjacent E and N inside the word are opponents; swapping them gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnet is the classic object that attracts things, here iron rather than spies.

clue.text: Bikini maybe excessively abbreviated all around

indicators.note: around tells us one word wraps itself about the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an abbreviated word is shortened by losing its final letter

parts.note: too means to an excessive degree

explanation.surface: A swimsuit that is far too skimpy all over.
explanation.walkthrough: Bikini is not the swimsuit but the Pacific atoll where the US tested atomic bombs, after which the swimsuit was named.
explanation.definitionFit: Bikini Atoll in the Marshall Islands is a ring-shaped coral reef, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Site not without oxygen, a biological supplier of nutrients

indicators.note: without signals taking away the chemical symbol for that element

parts.note: a site is a place
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A location starved of oxygen, described like a textbook diagram.
explanation.walkthrough: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen, removed from the middle word.
explanation.definitionFit: The placenta is the organ that passes nutrients from mother to foetus during pregnancy.

clue.text: "No" irrelevant before "yes"

parts.note: N/A, not applicable, as written on forms
Y is the abbreviation for yes on a form

explanation.surface: A refusal that doesn't matter once agreement arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Nay is an old-fashioned word for no, still used in voting.

clue.text: See 22
Rudely yawn, overwhelming otherwise laid-back Christian type

indicators.note: laid back means lying flat the other way, so the word is read from its end
to overwhelm is to engulf, so one set of letters swallows the other
done rudely means done roughly and without care, so the letters are knocked about

parts.note: taken as written
else means otherwise

explanation.surface: A churchgoer who is normally relaxed yawns impolitely during the sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wesleyan is a Methodist, a follower of John Wesley, so a type of Christian.

clue.text: Two whiskeys, one not completely dry

indicators.note: a word not completely there has lost its final letter

parts.note: Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet; this is the first of the two
the second whiskey is rye, the American grain spirit

explanation.surface: Someone orders a couple of whiskeys, one of them barely dry.
explanation.walkthrough: The two whiskeys are given two different ways: once as the radio-alphabet letter and once as a kind of whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: Wry humour is dry and mocking, so the words are synonyms in that sense.

clue.text: Basic report of three successive letters on time for each pupil

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so we take what the words sound like

parts.note: L, M and N follow one another in the alphabet
T is the abbreviation for time
a as in five pounds a head, meaning per
L is for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A school report saying each pupil got three letters in a row on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemental means fundamental or primary, which is what basic means.

clue.text: Man perhaps going after a bride might be here

parts.note: taken as written
the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A man pursues a bride to the place where she might be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like the groom, but it is the island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride walks up the aisle, the central passage of the church, on the way to her wedding.

clue.text: Dirty old man possibly put inside by Stormy

indicators.note: put inside means placed within the letters of what follows

parts.note: taken as written
one who lusts, which a dirty old man might be

explanation.surface: A lecherous old man is jailed by someone called Stormy.
explanation.definitionFit: Blustery weather is gusty and wild, which describes a stormy day.

clue.text: Milk consumption

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to exploit, as in milking a situation
second meaning: the using up of something

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a phrase about dairy intake, but milk is the verb meaning exploit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb meaning take advantage of and a noun meaning the act of consuming.

clue.text: Distributions by those willing to supply cars

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what people making a will leave to be shared out
second meaning: estate cars, the British term for station wagons

explanation.surface: Volunteers hand out vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those willing' looks like volunteers, but it means people who make wills; an estate car is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A deceased person's property shared out under their will forms their estate; estate cars are long-bodied vehicles.

clue.text: Be so good as to place conclusions of committee and referee in speech

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken out loud, so we write what we hear

parts.note: Pl. is the abbreviation for Place in street addresses

indicators.note: conclusions are endings, so each word gives only its final character

parts.note: both words end in E, and two Es said out loud match this spelling

explanation.surface: A polite request to a referee to set out the committee's findings.
explanation.definitionFit: Please, as in please sit down, is a courteous request meaning be so kind as to.

clue.text: Chromatic element of my prior ocular failing (fragmentary lights in rows)

indicators.note: something failing is breaking down, so the letters fall apart and regroup

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's former eyesight problem left them unable to see a basic colour.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed note tells the solver the answer is split into pieces across lights in different rows of the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A primary colour, such as red or blue, is a basic building block from which other colours are mixed.

clue.text: Big booby's little bird

parts.note: great means large
a tit is British slang for a fool, as is booby

explanation.surface: A large fool owns a small bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booby' looks like the seabird, but it means an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: The great tit is a common small European songbird, despite its name.

clue.text: Port in Germany? Why not wine?

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a major port
why not means yes, and yes in German is ja

explanation.surface: Someone is offered port in Germany and answers: why not have wine instead?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the fortified wine, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: Something hopped right on your toes

parts.note: beer is flavoured with hops
RT is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Something hops right onto your feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alert means watchful and ready, exactly what the idiom on your toes describes.

clue.text: Nibble at a steak, you won't want it all

indicators.note: you only want part of the phrase, so the solution sits inside the run of letters

parts.note: found running across the words

explanation.surface: Pick at a steak if you aren't hungry enough to finish it.
explanation.definitionFit: A taste is a small sample of food, the same as a nibble.

clue.text: Cool chaps could be killers in Brooklyn

parts.note: to ice something is to cool it
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Laid-back guys from Brooklyn may turn out to be hitmen.
explanation.walkthrough: To ice someone is American slang for killing them, so an iceman is a contract killer.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceman is American underworld slang for a hitman, hence the New York setting.

clue.text: Sat on extremely noncompliant capybara?

parts.note: a rider sits on the horse

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the two ends of the word

parts.note: first and last letters of noncompliant

explanation.surface: Someone sat on a stubborn giant guinea pig.
explanation.definitionFit: The capybara of South America is the largest gnawing mammal, an example signalled by the question mark.

clue.text: Surprised prostitute in vehicle with runners

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: a sled glides on runners
tart is slang for a prostitute

explanation.surface: A shocked sex worker on a sleigh.
explanation.definitionFit: Startled means taken by surprise and briefly alarmed.

clue.text: Starts to enter the chamber, it's obvious what comes next

indicators.note: starts are beginnings, so each word gives up its opening character

parts.note: initials of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone stepping into a council chamber knows exactly what will happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera is written when the rest of a list is predictable and needn't be spelt out.

clue.text: Where the font is waffled at by priest

indicators.note: to waffle is to ramble incoherently, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A priest rambles on at someone near the christening basin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Font' looks like typography, but it is the basin of holy water used for baptism.
explanation.definitionFit: A baptistery is the part of a church, or separate building, that houses the baptismal font.

clue.text: You previously turned back, abandoning obsequious servant in need

indicators.note: turned back means facing the other way, so read the word from its end
abandoning means leaving behind, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: a lackey is a servile follower
ye is the archaic form of you

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned master turns away, leaving a fawning servant destitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack and need are synonyms as nouns: a want or shortage of something.
